entities.summary:
Amazon.com, Inc. is an American multinational technology company founded by Jeff Bezos in 1994 in Bellevue, Washington, originally as an online bookstore. It expanded rapidly to become the world's largest e-commerce platform and cloud computing provider, fundamentally restructuring global retail, logistics, and digital infrastructure.

Amazon's expansion from books to 'everything store' disrupted traditional retail across every category, driving thousands of brick-and-mortar stores to close. Amazon Web Services (AWS), launched in 2006, created the cloud computing industry and now powers a significant portion of the global internet, from Netflix to the CIA. The company's relentless focus on customer experience and long-term investment over short-term profit became the defining corporate philosophy of the internet age.

By 2023, Amazon employed over 1.5 million people worldwide, operated the world's most advanced logistics network, and ran Prime, Alexa, Kindle, and Whole Foods among dozens of businesses. AWS alone generates more profit than the entire retail division. Amazon's supply chain innovations — one-day delivery, warehouse robotics, drone delivery research — set logistics standards globally, while its algorithmic pricing and marketplace model transformed how goods are bought and sold.
